Scholarship overview

UCL’s EPSRC Doctoral Landscape Awards support advertised engineering and physical sciences PhD projects. The 2027/28 catalogue and application route are expected to open in October 2026.

Research Areas

  • Engineering and physical sciences

Funding and duration

ComponentDetails
FundingHome fees plus a UCL award covering the Overseas fee difference; Research Training Support Grant.
MaintenanceExpected GBP 26,022/year for 2027/28; not final
Duration4 years

Eligibility and Requirements

Home and Overseas applicants who meet project and department entry requirements. International funded places are limited. English evidence, approved equivalents and waivers depend on the programme; IELTS is not a universal requirement for every applicant.

Application dates

ComponentDetails
RecruitmentOpening expected 26 October 2026
Deadline8 January 2027, noon UK; recruitment expected to open 26 October 2026

How to Apply

After opening, select an advertised UELA project and use the application link in the official catalogue.

UCL’s current prospective-student guidance gives an expected enhanced stipend of GBP 26,022; an older page gives GBP 24,522. Confirm the final rate.

About University College London

University College London offers postgraduate research across a broad range of disciplines. Its EPSRC doctoral funding supports engineering and physical sciences projects, with project-specific supervision and research training.

Official details: Programme information

Application route: Application form or official instructions

2026/27 UKRI reference rate: the minimum UKRI doctoral stipend is £21,805 per year, tax-free (London institutions +£2,000), effective 1 October 2026.
